# M4 Hardware history extraction

Date: 2026-10-27, Asia/Saigon. Original source and target Git refs were not changed. No stage, authored commit, merge, push or force option.

Environment: Windows/PowerShell, Git `2.52.0.windows.1`, Python `3.14.4`. The shared external session uses owner `netcircuit-m4` and explicit Remote, Hardware, Contracts and Simulator roots; child temporary directories and pip cache were set externally before tool installation.

At history preflight, Remote had only the coordinating agent's untracked M4 plan; Hardware was clean. Both indexes were empty. Concurrent ordinary implementation changes appeared afterward, while exact before/after source and target HEADs, named refs and staged state matched. Bundles snapshot committed refs, not that concurrent working tree.

- Source: `0d038c7aed15798696223558b4e58f5ffe926aa9` on `codex/m4-hardware-consumer`. Target initial: `2b0005f40dc826bc7940cd0af28c57ebb063fcb7` on `codex/m4-hardware-extract`. Filtered tip: `74ef21600c8c829667fc62b0fbd1a1d4b030a167`.
- Exact Git mode/type/blob parity: 21 entries at the selected source tip; every retained commit tree also matches its mapped original after path transformation.
- 22 retained commits from 126 mappings. Raw author and committer identity, epoch timestamp and timezone match for every retained mapping.
- git-filter-repo 2.47.0 installed in the owned external session. Fresh `git clone --no-local`; no `--force`.
- Followed all 21 historical selected file paths with `git log --all --follow --name-status`; no unselected predecessor path was found.
- Each of three durable bundles passed `git bundle verify`, actual restoration to a separate external mirror clone, expected HEAD checks, restoration of every advertised tip and `git fsck --full --strict`.
- Source and target initial histories remain separate. Connecting ancestry requires a separately authorized merge/commit. A snapshot commit alone does not connect ancestry.

## Exact path mapping and mixed-test provenance

- `services/hardware-service/**` → repository root (prefix removed).
- `.github/workflows/hardware-service.yml` and `LICENSE` retain their paths.
- `tests/fpga/test_lab_first_control.py` → `historical-only/tests/fpga/test_lab_first_control.py` **only in the filtered history bundle**. This preserves the original whole mixed transport/FPGA test blob and its history without presenting it as current product tests. It must not be copied into the Hardware product or collected as a standalone test. The full source bundle remains the unmodified anchor for its original path and surrounding FPGA context.
- Product transport assertions are split separately by ordinary source changes; this extraction does not rewrite mixed-test contents or claim unrelated FPGA code as Hardware ownership.

Session cleanup is coordinated by the parent migration task after all consumers finish; durable bundles are outside that cleanup scope.

## Reproduction and limits

Create source and initial-target archives with `git bundle create ABSOLUTE_BUNDLE --all`. In the fresh external source clone run:

```text
python SESSION/history-tools/git_filter_repo.py --path services/hardware-service/ --path-rename services/hardware-service/: --path .github/workflows/hardware-service.yml --path LICENSE --path tests/fpga/test_lab_first_control.py --path-rename tests/fpga/test_lab_first_control.py:historical-only/tests/fpga/test_lab_first_control.py
```

Filtering changes commit IDs, prunes unrelated commits, and may simplify topology. The table below is the complete filter-produced mapping, including pruned entries. The archives contain committed refs; concurrent ordinary uncommitted product/documentation work is not a bundle backup. All tree comparisons use Git object metadata and IDs, independent of worktree line-ending conversion.

The initial restore harness used ordinary clones and assumed every advertised tip was a commit. The full source archive also has custom `refs/codex` tips pointing directly to trees. The corrected gate uses actual `git clone --mirror --no-local BUNDLE EXTERNAL_RESTORE.git` restorations, checks every named ref exactly from `git show-ref` and every advertised object with `git cat-file -e`, then runs strict fsck. Individual `rev-parse --verify` lookup of the longest checkpoint ref failed at the long Windows restore path; `show-ref` and `for-each-ref` enumerate that exact ref/object successfully. Mirror mode maps all source refs, as described in the [official Git clone documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-clone#Documentation/git-clone.txt---mirror). This mirror operation is confined to temporary restoration clones; no source/target mirror push was performed.
